h1: The 8 Best Office Chairs for Tall People of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Office Chairs for Tall People: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 office chairs for tall people scored on seat height, back height and weight capacity, from budget mesh to Steelcase Gesture.
summary: The Steelcase Gesture with Headrest is the best chair here for a tall frame, because the headrest actually reaches a tall person's head. The Steelcase Leap V2 is the best pick for a flexible, tall spine. On a budget, the SIHOO M57 gives a high mesh back and 3D armrests for under $200, and the GTPLAYER reaches the highest seat height at 22 inches. Taller than 6 ft 4 in? Check seat height first, because several chairs top out around 21.7 inches.
intro: Most office chairs are built around a 5 ft 9 in person. If you are 6 ft 3 in or taller, that shows up as knees above the hips, a backrest that ends at the shoulder blades and a headrest that props the back of your neck. It is a fit problem, not a comfort one, and pillows do not fix it.

So this ranking leads with the numbers that matter for height: maximum seat height, backrest height, and weight capacity. We then looked at adjustability, warranty and price. Scores follow spec sheets and owner reports, and several budget chairs top out lower than their listings suggest.

products.name: Steelcase Gesture + Headrest
products.verdict: The Gesture with an adjustable headrest that reaches a tall person's head.
products.description:
The Gesture is built around a 3D LiveBack lumbar that flexes with the spine, and this version adds an adjustable headrest with height and angle control. For a tall person, that headrest is the missing piece, since fixed headrests on standard chairs end at the shoulders.

It costs the most in this guide and the headrest adds bulk. Against the plain Gesture it is the better tall fit, and against the Leap V2 it offers arms that move through 360 degrees, which suits people who use a laptop, tablet and phone through the day. A 12-year warranty backs it.

Buy it if you are tall, work eight hours a day and will pay once for a chair that actually fits.
products.idealFor: Tall full-time desk workers who want a chair that fits for years.
products.skipIf: You only sit a couple of hours a day.

products.name: Steelcase Leap V2 Office Chair
products.verdict: A flexible back with independent lower firmness that follows a long spine.
products.description:
The Leap V2 lets you set lower back firmness separately from upper back force, and its Natural Glide system keeps the chair moving with you. A longer torso needs that range, since a fixed curve will miss part of the spine.

It costs a lot and has no headrest at all, which is why it ranks below the Gesture with Headrest for the tallest users. What it offers in return is a flexible back that suits sitters who move around, plus height and width adjustable arms and a seat edge adjustment.

Best for tall users who do not need a headrest and value spine flexibility above everything else.
products.idealFor: Tall sitters who move a lot and do not need a headrest.
products.skipIf: You want a headrest built in.

products.name: Steelcase Gesture Office Chair
products.verdict: 3D LiveBack and 360 degree arms for people who spend eight hours or more seated.
products.description:
The Gesture is Steelcase's chair for heavy device use, with arms that follow your hands as you move between laptop, tablet and phone. The 3D LiveBack supports a tall spine as you recline or lean.

It costs less than the headrest version and ranks below it for tall users, since a tall head needs that extra support. It needs to be configured properly for a tall body, so set seat height and depth before judging it.

Best for tall people who use several devices and want premium support without paying for the headrest.
products.idealFor: Tall multi-device users who want premium support.
products.skipIf: You need head support at your height.

products.name: SIHOO Doro C300 Ergonomic Chair
products.verdict: An auto-following back and suspended mesh at a fraction of Steelcase pricing.
products.description:
The Doro C300 uses a backrest that follows your movement automatically, over suspended mesh that spreads pressure evenly. Seat depth is adjustable, which tall people need for long thighs.

It costs more than the other SIHOO chairs and the seat height tops out at 21.7 inches, which suits people up to about 6 ft 2 in. Compared with the Steelcase chairs, it saves a lot of money and gives up the long warranty (3 years).

Good for tall-ish users, around 6 feet to 6 ft 2 in, who want a mid-range upgrade.
products.idealFor: Users around 6 ft to 6 ft 2 in who want mid-range comfort.
products.skipIf: You are taller than about 6 ft 2 in.

products.name: SIHOO M57 Ergonomic Mesh Office Chair
products.verdict: High-back mesh, 3D armrests and an adjustable headrest for under $200.
products.description:
The M57 offers a high-back mesh backrest, adjustable lumbar and headrest, and 3D armrests, which is rare at its price. The mesh keeps tall sitters, who tend to run warm, cooler than foam.

Its 17.7 to 21.7 inch seat height range may fall short for users 6 ft 4 in and above. It ranks above the B100 because of the better arms and above the Marsail because of more height range.

A strong pick for tall buyers under 6 ft 3 in who want a real ergonomic chair on a modest budget.
cons: Seat height may be low at 6 ft 4 in+
products.idealFor: Tall buyers up to about 6 ft 3 in on a budget.
products.skipIf: You are 6 ft 4 in or taller.

products.name: SIHOO B100 Ergonomic Office Chair
products.verdict: A high backrest for long torsos at a low price.
products.description:
The B100 is a high-back mesh chair with adjustable lumbar, a headrest and 2D armrests. The tall backrest is its main appeal for people with long torsos.

The seat tops out at 21 inches, which is borderline for anyone 6 ft 3 in or taller, and the 2D armrests move less than the M57's 3D set. It is cheaper than the M57 and shares its 3-year warranty.

Best for tall buyers up to about 6 ft 2 in who want to spend as little as possible on a real mesh chair.
products.idealFor: Tall buyers up to 6 ft 2 in watching costs.
products.skipIf: You are 6 ft 3 in or taller.

products.name: GTPLAYER Gaming Chair with Footrest
products.verdict: A 22 inch seat height, 300 lb capacity and a retractable footrest.
products.description:
The GTPLAYER is the only chair here that reaches a 22 inch seat height, and it supports up to 300 lb. A retractable footrest and a recline from 90 to 160 degrees add comfort for gaming sessions.

It uses PU leather, which is less breathable than mesh, and the gaming look will not suit every office. It ranks below the mesh chairs for ergonomics because the lumbar and headrest are pillows, not built-in supports.

Best for tall gamers or home users who care about seat height and recline more than office styling.
products.idealFor: Tall gamers who need seat height and a deep recline.
products.skipIf: You need a professional office look or mesh breathability.

products.name: Marsail High Back Ergonomic Office Chair
products.verdict: The most affordable high-back mesh chair here, with flip-up arms.
products.description:
The Marsail is the cheapest high-back mesh chair in the guide, with adjustable lumbar, a headrest and flip-up armrests that save space under a desk.

Its seat height stops at 20 inches, the lowest of the group, and it has only a 1-year warranty. That makes it a poor fit for anyone above about 6 ft. The flip-up arms are also less adjustable than the 2D or 3D arms on the SIHOO chairs.

Only worth it for taller-than-average but not very tall buyers on the tightest possible budget.
products.idealFor: Slightly tall buyers on the tightest budget.

methodology.title: Seat height range
methodology.description: Maximum seat height decided most of the ranking, since a seat too low for long legs puts knees above the hips.

methodology.title: Back and head support
methodology.description: Backrest height, lumbar flexibility and headrest reach were checked against a tall torso and head.

methodology.title: Weight capacity
methodology.description: Capacity ratings were compared, since taller users often need more headroom on load.

methodology.title: Adjustability
methodology.description: Arms, seat depth and tilt controls were weighed for how much they let a tall body fine-tune the fit.

methodology.title: Warranty and value
methodology.description: Warranty length and price bracket were considered relative to the others in this guide.

whatMatters.detail: Seat height decides whether your feet reach the floor with knees at roughly a right angle. If your knees sit above your hips, the chair is too low. Check the maximum figure in the spec, and compare it to your own measurement from floor to the back of your knee.

A tall person needs a backrest that reaches the upper back and shoulders. Chairs with short backs leave the spine unsupported. Look for 'high-back' in the listing and compare listed back height to the distance from your seat to your shoulder blades.

A seat that is too short leaves your thighs unsupported. Seat depth adjustment lets you slide the seat forward so there is a couple of fingers of room behind the knee. It matters more for tall people than for anyone else.

Most fixed headrests land at shoulder level on a tall user. An adjustable headrest with height travel like the Steelcase Gesture + Headrest is the fix. Check how far the headrest rises, not just whether one is included.

Taller users are often heavier. A capacity rating of 300 lb or more gives margin. Cheap chairs may list a high rating but have thin mechanisms, so favour longer warranties as a proxy for build quality.

faq.q: What seat height do I need if I am 6 ft 4 in?
faq.a: Aim for a chair that goes above 21.7 inches, such as the GTPLAYER at 22 inches, or a Steelcase chair configured with the tall cylinder option. Check the listing carefully.

faq.q: Do tall people need a higher backrest?
faq.a: Yes. A short back leaves the upper spine unsupported. High-back mesh chairs like the SIHOO M57 reach higher than standard task chairs.

faq.q: Is a Steelcase worth it for a tall person?
faq.a: If you are very tall and sit all day, yes. The Gesture + Headrest solves the headrest reach problem and carries a 12-year warranty.

faq.q: Is a gaming chair a good option for tall users?
faq.a: It can be for seat height. The GTPLAYER reaches 22 inches and holds 300 lb, but the pillow lumbar and PU leather are weaker ergonomically than mesh.

faq.q: How should I set my seat height?
faq.a: Set it so your feet sit flat and your knees are at roughly a right angle, then adjust the desk or armrests to match.

faq.q: Does weight capacity matter for tall people?
faq.a: It often does. Choose 300 lb or more for margin, and prefer chairs with longer warranties.

finalTake: The Steelcase Gesture + Headrest is the best office chair for tall people, because it is the only one with a headrest that reaches and a 12-year warranty. The Leap V2 is the pick for a long, flexible spine. On a budget, the SIHOO M57 delivers the best mix of back height and adjustability, as long as you are under about 6 ft 3 in.
